compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The MCP server's code workspace is cloned once and then never updated, so every gate it runs reads a frozen tree that drifts further from `main` every day.

The workspace is the docker volume `gerrit_mcp_code`, mounted into the MCP container at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` and passed as both `MCP_CODE_DIR` and `REBAR_ROOT` (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:399-408`). `REBAR_ROOT` is the tree the completion-verifier and plan-review gates inspect when they check whether work is present in the repository.

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` clones that directory only when it is missing or its `HEAD` does not resolve — it requires both signals before re-cloning (around lines 128-130), and clones at line 163. There is no `fetch` and no `merge --ff-only` on an existing valid checkout. `autodeploy.sh` only mounts the volume; it never touches the checkout inside it. So once the clone succeeds, nothing in the system ever advances it again.

## Evidence

Observed on the prod host `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` on 2026-09-17:

- `gerrit_mcp_code` was on branch `main` at `665d1d0480`, clean, **130 commits behind** `origin/main`.
- Its reflog shows a `merge origin/main: Fast-forward` on 2026-09-07 23:36 and a `clone` on 2026-08-27, and nothing since. The 09-07 advance was manual; the gap is not explained by the review-bot pause, which began 2026-09-11.
- Concretely: `rebar transition f920-dc37-28e4-4a91 in_progress closed` failed with 6 unmet criteria, each reporting the work absent from the tree. The verifier said so explicitly: "the current HEAD (665d1d0480...) does not contain these changes." The work was in fact merged and was the tip of `origin/main` at the time.

## Impact

This silently corrupts the close and claim gates, which are the project's two certified operations.

- **False failures.** A ticket whose work has genuinely merged cannot be closed, because the verifier cannot see it. The failure text invites the operator to re-record evidence or to `--force`, and both responses are wrong — the evidence is real and the tree is stale. Agents are forbidden from using `--force`, so the correct-looking escape hatch is also unavailable, and the work simply cannot be closed.
- **False passes are possible in the other direction.** A criterion satisfied by code that has since been deleted or reworked on `main` still verifies against the frozen tree.
- The drift is unbounded and grows silently. Nothing reports it, and the gate output attributes the failure to the ticket rather than to the workspace.

## Approach

Refresh the workspace on the same cadence that already reflects `main` on the box, and make staleness observable rather than silent.

- Advance the checkout as part of the deploy path that already runs every ~2 minutes and already knows the target commit — `autodeploy.sh` logs `up to date (<sha>); no-op` against exactly the SHA the workspace should be on.
- The update must be a `fetch` plus `merge --ff-only`. A non-fast-forward or a dirty tree must fail loud and leave the workspace untouched, consistent with the existing `declared-service-down; decision=fail-loud-no-auto-restart` posture: silently resetting a workspace a gate may be mid-read on would trade one correctness bug for another.
- Portability constraint: this must not be triggered only by a specific CI provider. The refresh belongs to the deploy/entrypoint path on the box, which is where the workspace lives, so it holds for any environment that runs the MCP server.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` — fetch and fast-forward an existing valid `MCP_CODE_DIR` instead of only re-cloning a broken one.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — advance the workspace when reconciling the MCP service, so drift cannot exceed one tick.
- A test covering the refresh decision: valid-and-behind fast-forwards, dirty or diverged fails loud without mutating, missing or unresolvable `HEAD` still re-clones.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — document the workspace, how to check its drift, and the manual fast-forward as the break-glass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An existing, clean `MCP_CODE_DIR` that is behind `origin/main` is fast-forwarded to the deploy target rather than left frozen.
- [ ] A dirty or diverged workspace is not mutated and the condition is reported loudly.
- [ ] A missing workspace, or one whose `HEAD` does not resolve, is still re-cloned exactly as today.
- [ ] Drift is observable: the deploy path emits the workspace SHA and its distance from the target.
- [ ] Tests cover all four decisions above.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` documents the workspace, the drift check, and the manual fast-forward.

## Interim state

The workspace was fast-forwarded by hand to unblock two closes in this session, first to `e5293bf5b14` and then to `e46d03aa83c`. That is a manual mitigation of a single symptom, not a fix: with nothing automated, it will freeze again at whatever commit was current when the last person happened to intervene.
compiled_state.title: MCP code workspace is cloned once and never refreshed, so completion and plan-review gates verify a stale tree
